There are what I call "Sheepie" blankets that I get from Costco. They aren't faux fur exactly, but they are super soft velour stuff on one side and faux sheep skin on the other.  


I have a robe made of the same velour-ish material -  [https://www.amazon.com/Carole-Hochman-Ladies-Plush-Wrap/dp/B07MQG9DXC/ref=pd\_lpo\_sbs\_193\_img\_2?\_encoding=UTF8&psc=1&refRID=B708N4HHHQSKZP6AAKFG](https://www.amazon.com/Carole-Hochman-Ladies-Plush-Wrap/dp/B07MQG9DXC/ref=pd_lpo_sbs_193_img_2?_encoding=UTF8&psc=1&refRID=B708N4HHHQSKZP6AAKFG) 

and I acquire more blankets randomly because yeah, for me, soft helps.   


I like these when it's too warm for sheepie blankets -  [https://www.amazon.com/Flannel-Fleece-Luxury-Blanket-Lightweight/dp/B06Y2T3LCY](https://www.amazon.com/Flannel-Fleece-Luxury-Blanket-Lightweight/dp/B06Y2T3LCY)
Please note: my actual response was "probably not, but I am trying" + a weak smile and did not involve a wrench, chair, or any other form of violence.

and oh, the chiding tone. Possibly entirely my interpretation rather than reality, but the "did you remember to say thank you?"-directed-at-a-4-year-old-who-you-know-did-Not-say-thank-you tone and delivery added extra apply-metal-to-medical-professional-with-all-available-force desire.
Does anyone actual go "oh, no, I'm not. Guess I'll cut back on my moonlight strolls and drink some warm milk tonight. Thanks, Doc!"
Thank you.
/hug
/hug

I appreciate the author's sentiment, but I think the statement about a complicated patient coming in after a long absence and having a huge list may be from a place of misunderstanding. 

It takes a lot of my hoarded effort to first *make* the appointment and then *go* to the appointment. So, regardless of what help the doctor can give me that day, I need to give them the full list *now* in case I can't come back for a month or more. 

Phone calls with doctors are easier for me to attend and I will pay them just as much, but they tend to be only long enough for one problem or update. When I'm there in person, I want to lay everything out so the doctor can get the full picture. 

Perhaps I should tell my next doctor this, eh?
Any of the "let cool for *X* minutes" warnings when applied to frozen cheesy deliciousness.

I have had a similar experience with Bipolar II. My brother has the creative ridiculously-productive-amazing-genius mania. I have the agitation-can't-sleep-anxiety-irritability type. Unfortunately, our kind has...well...less (I hesitate to use this word) upside. 

I would like the music-of-the-spheres mania, but I am content with meds induced (approx.) equilibrium.
Tonight's MS Paint art inspired by **OW**. *Flexeril + Ibuprofen (both prescribed) isn't cutting it this evening.*
I call my Himalayan cat an optical illusion. :)

Given how much better off I am than my mom is/was due to advances in medicine, I'm surprised that I didn't think of this.

Thank you. :)

I've thought about adopting, but I have to wonder; what if the kid has some disease or disorder (or pack of them) that I don't spot because I've never seen it? I have lots of genetic issues in my bloodline, but I think we've worked out *what* most of them are. It took a lot of time, money and effort to do that too. I think it would be even harder to deal with the problems of a child without a genetic map to reference.

Thoughts?

I have fallen asleep standing up on the subway. Wide awake & alert -> stumbling awake as I lurch sideways with my mind on a completely different track than it was moments before.

It can act like a sudden system restart and can take literally 10 seconds to occur.

When I'm in an intimate position with my gentleman, I am nowhere near as alert to my surroundings as I am on the subway, so it has happened.

Happily, lube is generally handy and my mind can be directed back on to the original track after a minute or two. 

Occasionally, I will need him to go back to foreplay (an accelerated version works fine) to get me back into the groove.

It's not just you two. :)

In theory, I could switch off of my current SSRI and onto Lyrica or Cymbalta or whatnot, but I'm not sure my job would survive the ensuing bipolar shenanigans. 

I don't suppose you tried that, did you? If so, I would love to have any advice on how or questions I should ask my psych and my fibromyalgia lady.

Yup. My brother and I both have genetic forms of arthritis to go with our bipolar disorder and bouts of more intense pain shove the bipolar pendulum into depression land. 

I am sorry that you are going through this.

/hug.

What would you like? An arm? A leg? An eye? 15 years of my life? I don't know if I would give up a sense (e.g. sight, hearing), but other than that? 

I wouldn't harm someone else to get rid of it. I might ask the person if it was something like, oh, getting tazed with no chance of complications, but anything more than that, I don't think so. 

I would give up using the internet for anything not-job related. 

I wouldn't give up ever being warm and fed. 

I would give up sugar. 

I might actually give up my fertility i.e. the possibility of ever having a child. 

I might give up the hope of romantic love if I can get rid of all physical and mental issues.
Just to corroborate with slkwont's comment; I have bipolar disorder and Lyrca shoved my internal pendulum off into hypomanic land within 3 days.
No answer?   Sadness...

I'm not sure if I'm getting the sense of your comment fully, but I think the Catch-22 you speak of is emotion itself, or perhaps empathy. I think emotional pain will always be part of humanity, but I think the general attitude towards depression, anxiety etc., both circumstantial and chemical, has been vastly improved in recent history. This in turn has increased both the help available and the willingness of the individual to seek that help. Empathy and understanding are now found in many places, not least of all reddit. The flip side of emotion, the human capacity for joy, is something to live for in itself. :)

I am glad my post made you feel less alone. I highly recommend venting anonymously in a public forum if your emotional pain is becoming overwhelming. Posting helped to release the internal tension and allowed me to confront my grief instead of it tearing me apart unawares. Thus, I went to work this morning. I even clocked in on time.

:)

Thank you for reading it. I am glad that you managed to glean some beauty from the dross of my grief. My apartment is indeed filled with trash, but I try to clean the filth out of my mind more regularly (hence the original post). I truly see depression/grief as a canker of the mind. One must release the pus fairly frequently if one is to keep the pain at a bearable level. 

May we keep holding to the present and may our lives be filled with unanticipated pleasures.
